Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the 24 * rule for deciding when two owners denote the same person lives in one place, as pure functions 25 * with no web or persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer}, 26 * {@link EmailNormalizer} and {@link HouseholdNormalizer}, whose comparison keys it composes. 27 * 28 *

The key is the owner's normalized telephone, email (or the empty string when absent) and 29 * household id joined with {@code '|'} separators: 30 * {@code normalizedTelephone + '|' + email + '|' + householdId}. Two owners are the same, and a 31 * create is rejected as a {@code 409 Conflict}, only when their whole keys are equal — so the 32 * previously separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks are all subsumed by this one 33 * key. Because the telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same 34 * {@code householdId}) with different telephones have different keys and are both allowed; only an 35 * exact full-key match is a duplicate. 36 */ 37 public abstract class OwnerIdentity { 38 39 /** Separates the telephone, email and household components of the key. */ 40 private static final String SEPARATOR = "|"; 41 42 /** 43 * Builds the identity key from an owner's raw parts. The telephone and email are reduced to 44 * their {@linkplain TelephoneNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} / 45 * {@linkplain EmailNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} forms so values stored in different 46 * shapes still compose equal keys; an absent (null or blank) email contributes the empty string, 47 * and an absent household id likewise contributes the empty string. 48 * 49 * @param telephone the owner's telephone (normalized on create), or null 50 * @param email the owner's email (lower-cased on create), or null/blank when absent 51 * @param householdId the owner's household id, or null 52 * @return the owner's identity key 53 */ 54 public static String identityKey(String telephone, String email, String householdId) { 55 String telephonePart = telephone == null ? "" : TelephoneNormalizer.toComparisonKey(telephone); 56 String emailPart = (email == null || email.isBlank()) ? "" : EmailNormalizer.toComparisonKey(email); 57 String householdPart = householdId == null ? "" : householdId; 58 return telephonePart + SEPARATOR + emailPart + SEPARATOR + householdPart; 59 } 60 61 /** 62 * Builds the identity key from a persisted owner's stored telephone, email and household id. 63 * 64 * @param owner the owner (non-null) 65 * @return the owner's identity key 66 */ 67 public static String identityKey(Owner owner) { 68 return identityKey(owner.getTelephone(), owner.getEmail(), owner.getHouseholdId()); 69 } 70 71 } 72

1 /* 2 * Copyright 2016-2017 the original author or authors. 3 * 4 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); 5 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. 6 * You may obtain a copy of the License at 7 * 8 * http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 9 * 10 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software 11 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, 12 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. 13 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and 14 * limitations under the License. 15 */ 16 17 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util; 18 19 import java.util.Locale; 20 import java.util.Optional; 21 import java.util.Set; 22 import java.util.regex.Pattern; 23 24 /** 25 * Normalization and comparison of owner email addresses. Kept separate from the owner controller 26 * and the {@code Owner} model so the rules for shaping and comparing an email live in one place, 27 * as pure functions with no web or persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer} 28 * and {@link HouseholdNormalizer}, which do the same for telephones and households. 29 * 30 *

A submitted email is reduced to its canonical form — trimmed and lower-cased — which is the 31 * value stored and returned. The value is accepted only when it is a syntactically valid address. 32 * Two emails denote the same address when their {@linkplain #toComparisonKey(String) comparison 33 * keys} — their lower-cased forms — are equal. 34 */ 35 public abstract class EmailNormalizer { 36 37 /** 38 * Syntactic validation for an owner email: a non-empty local part, an '@', and a dotted domain 39 * whose top-level label is at least two letters. Deliberately conservative so plainly malformed 40 * input (e.g. a value without an '@') is rejected. 41 */ 42 private static final Pattern EMAIL_PATTERN = 43 Pattern.compile("^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$"); 44 45 /** 46 * Domains of disposable / throwaway email providers that an owner email is not permitted to use. 47 * Kept lower-cased so a submitted address, once reduced to its canonical (lower-cased) form, can be 48 * matched against this set directly. 49 */ 50 private static final Set DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS = 51 Set.of("mailinator.com", "tempmail.com", "guerrillamail.com"); 52 53 /** 54 * Reduce a submitted email to its canonical form — trimmed and lower-cased — which is the value 55 * to be stored and returned. The result is accepted only when the trimmed value is a 56 * syntactically valid address (see {@link #EMAIL_PATTERN}). 57 * 58 * @param rawEmail the submitted email (non-null) 59 * @return the canonical (trimmed, lower-cased) email, or {@link Optional#empty()} if 60 * {@code rawEmail} is not a syntactically valid address 61 */ 62 public static Optional normalize(String rawEmail) { 63 String email = rawEmail.trim(); 64 if (!EMAIL_PATTERN.matcher(email).matches()) { 65 return Optional.empty(); 66 } 67 return Optional.of(email.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)); 68 } 69 70 /** 71 * The key used to decide whether two emails denote the same address: the email's lower-cased 72 * form, so emails stored in different letter cases still compare equal. A value that is not a 73 * syntactically valid address (e.g. legacy data) falls back to its plain lower-cased form. 74 * 75 * @param email a stored or already-normalized email (non-null) 76 * @return the comparison key 77 */ 78 public static String toComparisonKey(String email) { 79 return normalize(email).orElseGet(() -> email.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)); 80 } 81 82 /** 83 * Whether the given email's domain is on the disposable-domain blocklist (see 84 * {@link #DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS}). The domain is the part after the last {@code '@'}, compared 85 * case-insensitively. A value with no {@code '@'} is treated as having no blocked domain. 86 * 87 * @param email a submitted or already-normalized email (non-null) 88 * @return {@code true} if the email's domain is on the blocklist 89 */ 90 public static boolean hasDisposableDomain(String email) { 91 int at = email.lastIndexOf('@'); 92 if (at < 0) { 93 return false; 94 } 95 String domain = email.substring(at + 1).toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT); 96 return DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS.contains(domain); 97 } 98 99 } 100

The build compiled cleanly and the test state is **exactly preserved** from baseline: `coreRejectsDuplicateIdentity` still passes, and the v2-only `coreIdentityKeyIsSha256Hex` still fails with the *identical* identityKey value (`+61400000004||11b2b2a3a9a7`) as before — confirming behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. That failing test is the acceptance criterion for the upcoming change, which I was told not to implement.

## What I did

The upcoming redesign would concentrate complexity in the spots flagged (a new SHA-256 hasher in `OwnerIdentity`, plus the duplicate-detection methods that must keep "ignoring deleted owners"). I made two behavior-preserving preparations so that change lands as ordinary code here.

**1. Extracted a shared `Sha256.hex(...)` util** (`util/Sha256.java`)

The codebase had **three** copies of the same SHA-256-to-hex logic: a private `sha256Hex` in `HouseholdNormalizer`, an identical one in `CustomerCode`, and the change was set to add a fourth in `OwnerIdentity` (one of the listed hotspots). I pulled it into a single `Sha256` abstract util — matching the existing `TelephoneNormalizer`/`EmailNormalizer`/`LuhnCheckDigit` convention (pure static functions, thorough Javadoc) — and routed `HouseholdNormalizer` and `CustomerCode` through it. When the new `identityKey` needs to hash `telephone|email|soundex(lastName)`, it now has a home to delegate to, the same way it already delegates normalization to its sibling utils — so no `OwnerIdentity::sha256Hex` copy is needed.

**2. Extracted `activeOwners()` in `OwnerRestControllerV1`**

All three duplicate-detection paths (`rejectDuplicateIdentity`, `rejectHouseholdDuplicate`, `findPossibleDuplicate`) repeated `findAllOwners().stream().filter(existing -> !existing.isDeleted())`. The change keeps "ignore owners flagged deleted" for both the 409 identity check and the soft match, so I unified that concept into one documented helper. The two hotspot methods (`rejectDuplicateIdentity`, `findPossibleDuplicate`) now open on `activeOwners().stream()...`, leaving room for the identity-key and soundex predicates to swap in cleanly.

## What I deliberately left alone

`Soundex::encode` and the reshaped `OwnerIdentity::identityKey` are the *core new logic* of the change — writing them would be implementing it, so they're out of scope. The util package's conventions are already clean and consistent, so a new `Soundex` class slots in next to the existing normalizers naturally when the change lands.
